reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that increasing boriding temperature and duration increases layer thickness, but it does not address layer density, continuity, diffusion barrier properties, or corrosion resistance in molten aluminum. The key premises about denser layers acting as diffusion barriers and reducing corrosion by 20–30% are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Increasing boriding temperature and duration increases boride layer thickness
A denser and more continuous boride layer acts as an enhanced diffusion barrier
An enhanced diffusion barrier reduces molten-aluminum corrosion rates
Optimized boriding can achieve a 20–30% reduction in corrosion relative to conventional boriding
The boride layer remains effective up to ~700 °C provided structural integrity is maintained
